newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil stable in U.S. holiday doldrums.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil stable in U.S. holiday doldrums.

text.p: European gas oil trade was mostly dormant on Thursday due to the U.S. holiday and spreads were discussed at stable levels.
July IPE gas oil futures slipped 75 cents to trade at $163.75 a tonne at 1132 GMT in line with weaker Brent.
Many traders around Europe were taking advantage of the U.S Independence Day holiday to leave for long weekends.

On the barge market sellers were asking a premium of 75 cents over July IPE for 0.2 percent sulphur heating oil for delivery in the first half of July, some 25 cents firmer than Thursday's levels as a result of the fall in futures.
Buyers were around flat to 25 cents over the futures price.
Offers were notionally at a premium of $1 over July IPE for second half July deliveries. Very little buying interest was seen for the second half of July.
Most buyers said they were holding off to await price direction on Monday when the U.S. market reopens.

On cargoes attention is focussed on the Mediterranean where the result of a Turkish tender for three 25,000 tonne cargoes of 0.7 percent sulphur gas oil is due to be announced. Traders have predicted prices at $10/12 over fob Med Italy price quotes.
